expectations.text: Includes a per-unit price and floor-plan table (beds, baths, m²/sq ft, price)

There is no beds or baths column, and no per-model beds/baths data anywhere in the doc — the only bed/bath mentions are generic prose ('65 m² one-bedroom' at line 17, and a 'HOA $227.50/month' / '1 bed/1 bath' fact that appears only in the transcript's research notes, not in output.md itself). expectations.text: The hook paragraph names one specific, verifiable fact about Bioma Costa del Este (a permit, license, developer track record, or price anomaly) rather than generic marketing language
expectations.evidence: Hook (output.md line 11): 'their previous tower, Dovle in Coco del Mar, reportedly sold 170 units in 19 hours' — a specific, checkable developer track-record claim, sourced in the sources list to La Prensa Panamá (line 139-141, checked_on 2026-07-30). The hook explicitly disclaims a permit/legal angle ('Bioma doesn't have a unique legal angle... no permit or title position here') rather than inventing one, and substitutes this verifiable sales-record fact plus a specific amenity figure (7,000+ m², podium levels 0-4) in its place.

expectations.text: At least one drawback is named and is attributed to a source other than the developer (UGC, forum, or reasoned risk) rather than a generic hedge like 'may not suit everyone'
expectations.evidence: drawbacks field (output.md line 77): the delivery-date drawback is a reasoned-risk finding built from cross-referencing an aggregator listing (Q4 2025) against The Agency Panama's broker page (2028-2029) and a SkyscraperCity excavation timeline — none of it developer-sourced marketing. A second drawback ('we could not locate a public, independently verifiable construction permit or Registro Público record') is an absence-of-verification finding, also not developer-attributed. Both are specific and reasoned, not the generic 'may not suit everyone' hedge the expectation warns against.

expectations.text: At least 3 FAQs are present, phrased as real buyer questions
expectations.evidence: output.md lines 89-108 contain 7 FAQs, each phrased as a first-person buyer question: 'How many floors does Bioma have?', 'What's the starting price at Bioma?', 'When will Bioma be delivered?', 'Who is the developer, and have they delivered projects before?', 'What are the HOA fees at Bioma?', 'Is Bioma titled property?', 'How far is Bioma from the airport?' — well above the 3-FAQ minimum and phrased naturally rather than as SEO keyword stuffing.

expectations.text: At least one figure (price, tax, or fee) carries a named source and a check date/month, not just a bare number
expectations.evidence: sources section (output.md lines 112-147) attaches a named source and checked_on date to every cited figure, e.g. 'RE/MAX Panama — Bioma listing (storeys, unit sizes, starting price), url: https://www.remax-panama.com/002602231062, checked_on: 2026-07-30' and 'The Agency Panama — Bioma at Costa del Este (architect, delivery estimate, deposit structure), checked_on: 2026-07-30'. In-body text also names sources inline, e.g. 'per The Agency Panama's listing: reservation deposits start at $1,000...' (buying_note, line 85) and 'based on Panama Equity's published rate' (line 31).

Searched output.md for 'approximately'/'approx.'/currency-conversion patterns. The only occurrences are 'Approx. price/m²' (a derived-metric table column, not a currency conversion) and 'Monthly HOA runs approximately $3.25-$3.50 per m², based on Panama Equity's published rate and an Encuentra24 listing showing $227.50/month' (line 31) — an approximation of a range that is explicitly sourced to two named listings, not an unsourced USD-to-other-currency conversion. No instance of the flagged pattern ('$X USD (approximately...)') appears anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Body prose (excluding the price table) is substantive, not a thin 150-word placeholder
expectations.evidence: The body field (output.md lines 13-69) runs to roughly 1,400+ words across five substantive subsections ('Bioma Costa del Este prices and floor plans', 'Where Bioma actually is', 'What's included at Bioma', 'Who Bioma suits — and who it doesn't', 'Before you buy at Bioma'), each with multiple sourced paragraphs and specific reconciled facts (price discrepancies, delivery-date conflict, deposit structure, amenity breakdown). claims.evidence: transcript.md documents all three failures explicitly ('thepanamalink.com/bioma/ — failed, HTTP 429', 'panacrypto.com/buildings/bioma/ — failed, HTTP 403', PDF 'not extractable in a useful way'), matching metrics.json's 'errors_encountered': 3.

suggestions.assertion: Includes a per-unit price and floor-plan table (beds, baths, m²/sq ft, price)
suggestions.reason: This is a compound assertion (four distinct data columns bundled into one pass/fail). The output fully satisfies half of it (a real per-model size/price table exists and is well-sourced) but omits beds/baths entirely, which forces an all-or-nothing FAIL on an otherwise strong table. Consider splitting into two assertions — 'includes a per-unit size/price table' and 'table includes bedroom/bathroom counts' — so partial credit is visible and future runs get more actionable feedback than a single opaque failure.

No assertion checks whether the numeric contradictions across sources (storey count, price, delivery date) are disclosed to the reader rather than silently resolved — this is arguably the single most impressive thing this output does (three separate, explicitly reconciled discrepancies with judgment calls stated in the open), and no expectation gives credit for it. Consider adding an assertion like 'when source figures conflict, the output discloses the conflict rather than presenting one number as settled fact' — it would be genuinely discriminating, since a weaker run would likely just pick a number and move on.

No assertion checks that drawbacks/claims of 'could not verify' are actually true absences rather than the writer having skipped a check. In this run the transcript shows real attempts (PDF fetch of the government permit registry, three UGC query rounds) before declaring the gap, but an eval could not distinguish that from an executor that never tried. Consider an assertion tied to the transcript specifically: 'unverified claims are preceded by a documented verification attempt, not just a bare disclaimer.'

eval_feedback.overall: 7 of 8 expectations pass with strong, specific evidence. The one failure (missing beds/baths in the floor-plan table) is a genuine, unambiguous gap — the table has model/size/price but no bedroom or bathroom counts anywhere in the document. The output's real strength (transparent handling of three separate cross-source numeric conflicts, and dropping a fabricated AI-summary statistic after verification) is not covered by any current assertion and is worth adding a check for.
